title: Three-way tradeoff routing playbook: latency / cost / reliability
content:
Purpose and scope
This note collects pragmatic decision logic for runtime routing that explicitly reasons about three competing objectives: latency (user-perceived delay), cost (per-request compute + infra spend), and reliability (success rates, graceful degradation). It is intended for the routing/control-plane owners and the SRE/product partners who tune SLOs and pricing policies.

Context and motivation
- We run heterogeneous capacity across regions and model variants (full-precision, quantized, distilled). Each candidate has a distinct latency distribution, unit cost, and historical reliability.
- Traffic should be routed to optimize for a request-level utility that reflects product intent (e.g., interactive chat vs nightly batch).
- Primary constraints to encode: data residency & compliance, capacity headroom, prioritized SLAs for paying customers.

High-level decision flow (plain-language)
1) Enrich request: attach metadata (customer_tier, max_cost_budget, latency_priority, data_region, model_hint, route_affinity).
2) Filter candidate set by hard constraints: data residency, allowed model families, explicit blacklists, and regional outages.
3) For each candidate (region+variant), compute a normalized triple: (latency_score, cost_score, reliability_score). Normalization uses rolling baselines (per-candidate medians and p95).
4) Compute a weighted utility U = w_L * f_L(latency_score) + w_C * f_C(cost_score) + w_R * f_R(reliability_score). We pick the candidate with highest U.
5) If U < safe_threshold for all candidates and fallback is allowed, route to a conservative fallthrough (cheapest stable variant in primary region or multi-region replicated endpoint).
6) Emit telemetry (chosen_candidate, scores, candidate_ranking) for offline tuning and online observability.

Scoring primitives and normalization
- latency_score: maps observed p95 latency relative to SLO. Define latency_score in [0,1] where 1 is ideal (latency << SLO) and 0 is unacceptable (latency > SLO * 3). Use a smooth transformation: latency_score = 1 / (1 + log(1 + (p95 / SLO))).
- cost_score: we prefer lower cost, so cost_score = 1 - normalize(cost_per_1k_tokens, min_cost, p99_cost). Clip to [0,1].
- reliability_score: based on success_rate and recent degradation signals (circuit-breaker state). reliability_score = success_rate * (1 - degradation_penalty).
Notes on baselines: compute min_cost and p99_cost per model family per region with a 7d sliding window. SLO values are per-customer-per-route configuration.

Weighting strategy (w_L, w_C, w_R)
- Default weights by request intent (examples):
  - interactive-low-latency: w_L=0.6, w_C=0.2, w_R=0.2
  - cost-sensitive-batch: w_L=0.1, w_C=0.7, w_R=0.2
  - enterprise-sla: w_L=0.4, w_C=0.1, w_R=0.5
- Weights come from route-level config and can be controlled at customer level or product route.
- Safety note: reliability weight should never be zero for critical routes (min w_R = 0.1).

Decision tree examples (text-format)
A) Interactive chat, gold customer, region US-WEST, latency SLO = 150ms, cost_budget = high
  1) Candidate set: us-west-gpu:fp32, us-west-gpu:quant, us-east-gpu:fp32 (cross-region fallthrough)
  2) Scores computed -> utility picks us-west-gpu:fp32 (meets p95 << SLO)
  3) If primary candidate p95 spikes above SLO*1.5 and reliability_score drops below 0.85, failover to us-west-gpu:quant (lower cost, slightly higher latency) with a canary ratio 10% -> 100% over 60s if healthy.
B) Low-priority embedding batch from EU: latency SLO = 10s, cost_budget = low
  1) Candidate set: eu-cpu:quant, eu-gpu:quant, global-batch-cluster
  2) Weighted for cost so choose eu-cpu:quant or global-batch which has much lower cost per vector.
  3) If queue backlog > 2x and eu-cpu latency > 2*SLO, spillover to global-batch and mark request trace for possible retry.

Fallback and degradation modes
- Graceful degradation hierarchy:
  1) model_variant downgrade (fp32 -> quant -> distilled) in-region
  2) regional fallthrough (same variant, different region) if capacity but higher latency acceptable
  3) global pooled batch cluster for low-priority work
- Each fallback must be accompanied by: a) telemetry tag b) customer-visible header when applicable c) cost-accounting attribution.

Control-plane primitives required
- Candidate catalog service: per model variant metadata (median latency, p95, unit_cost, capacity, last_health)
- Real-time signal bus: fresh p95, error rates, queue depths per endpoint (<=10s granularity)
- Policy engine: evaluates the utility model and enforces hard filters (data residency, blacklists)
- Rollout governor: supports canaries, gradual traffic shifts, and automated rollback on regret metrics

Safety and operational constraints
- Never route outside of declared data residency for requests marked "must-stay-local".
- For routes with an explicit SLA, enforce min reliability weight and a conservative fallback budget.
- Inject jitter and randomized tie-breaking to avoid thundering herd when multiple candidates equal utility.

Tuning and automated learning options
- Bandit tuning: treat variants as arms and use an epsilon-greedy or Thompson sampling strategy to tune w_C/w_L per route while enforcing safety floor constraints (no more than 5% exploratory traffic on SLA-critical routes).
- Offline cost-latency frontier builder: compute Pareto front of candidates for each route and region; surface nondominated options in console to tune defaults.
- Auto-adjust weights via simple PID controls on cost drift vs target and p95 vs SLO. Keep PID output bounded to avoid oscillation.

Monitoring and key metrics to surface
- Per-route: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, cost_per_1k_tokens, success_rate, fallback_rate, rollback_events
- Candidate-level: recent capacity headroom, instant error spikes, queued_requests
- Business: cost_per_customer, SLA_violations_by_tier, region_cost_breakdown

Example utility computation (numbers)
- Route intent: interactive-low-latency (w_L=0.6, w_C=0.2, w_R=0.2)
- Candidate A: p95=120ms (SLO 150ms) -> latency_score=0.8; cost=$0.12/1k -> cost_score=0.6; reliability=0.99 -> reliability_score=0.99
  U_A = 0.6*0.8 + 0.2*0.6 + 0.2*0.99 = 0.48 + 0.12 + 0.198 = 0.798
- Candidate B: p95=160ms -> latency_score=0.45; cost=$0.06/1k -> cost_score=0.9; reliability=0.995 -> reliability_score=0.995
  U_B = 0.6*0.45 + 0.2*0.9 + 0.2*0.995 = 0.27 + 0.18 + 0.199 = 0.649
- Choose A even though B is cheaper because latency weight dominates.

Pseudocode (simplified)
- function route(request):
    meta = enrich(request)
    candidates = catalog.lookup(meta.model_hint, meta.data_region)
    candidates = filter_hard_constraints(candidates, meta)
    scored = []
    for c in candidates:
      latency_s = score_latency(c.p95, meta.SLO)
      cost_s = score_cost(c.cost)
      reli_s = score_reliability(c.success_rate, c.circuit_breaker)
      U = meta.w_L*latency_s + meta.w_C*cost_s + meta.w_R*reli_s
      scored.append((c, U))
    best = argmax(scored)
    if best.U < meta.safe_threshold and meta.allow_fallback:
      return fallback_route(meta)
    else:
      return best.endpoint

Testing and rollout guidance
- Start with conservative reliability and latency weights, enable full telemetry. Run in shadow mode for 48–72 hours before live rollout.
- Use canaries: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated halt on p95 increase > 20% or error_rate > 0.5% over baseline.
- Backfill historic traces via simulator to validate chosen weights across seasonal traffic patterns.

Open questions and follow-ups
- How to incorporate subjective quality regressions (model quality) into the reliability_score in a timely way? Proposal: add an eval-based quality_penalty signal when the model's recent prompt-set scores drop beyond threshold.
- How aggressive should cross-region failovers be for low-latency routes? Current heuristic: prefer in-region downgrade for first fallback, cross-region only if variant downgrade still violates reliability or capacity.
- Bandit exploration windows: empirically validate 12h vs 72h windows for stable conclusions.

Appendix: quick checklist before enabling a new route policy
- Catalog entries exist for all candidate endpoints with recent telemetry
- Weights and SLOs documented on the route config
- Linked rollback and on-call runbook referenced
- Shadow testing completed for at least 48h
- Alert thresholds set for p95, cost drift, and fallback rate

This doc is intentionally pragmatic and algorithm-light to be actionable for engineers tuning the control plane. Comments and edits welcome — leave notes inline or ping the author.
